name: Five Spice Turkey Noodle Bowls
writer_notes: SELECTOR: Verified source: full recipe, 4 servings, 290 cal / 35g protein - the best protein-per-calorie number in the slice. Confidence note: as published it is a brothy bowl well under 500 cal, so ours needs to be a thicker noodle bowl with more noodles to qualify. Five-spice is board-tracked and nothing live uses it. | HARVEST:
intro_html: Five spice powder is one of those seasonings that does more work than it has any right to: star anise, cinnamon, clove, fennel, and pepper in one spoonful. Here it seasons ground turkey and mushrooms in a brothy noodle bowl finished with hot honey, which brings sweet heat to the back end. Each bowl comes to 561 calories and 34 grams of protein for about $4.84 (at everyday cost).
ingredients_display: Lo Mein Noodles (Simply Asia): 45.5 oz dry (1293 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Chicken Broth, 3.4 cartons: ~$4.26. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 4 32oz cartons.
Lo Mein Noodles, 45.5 oz dry: ~$4.96. Buy 4 14oz packs: $6.09.
Pantry seasonings (five-spice powder, salt, black pepper): ~$2.93. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $35.94 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.57 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $40.38 across 14 servings, roughly $2.88 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $24.41 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $64.79. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About $4.84 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a noodle bowl with real depth to it. The five spice jar in your cabinet is what makes the difference, and it costs pennies per serving.
shop_smart: Mushrooms are the second biggest line here. Buy them the day they get marked down, because slightly wrinkled mushrooms actually taste more concentrated once they hit a hot pan.

Broth is a real line for this batch because a noodle bowl drinks a lot of it. Bouillon base dissolved in water costs a fraction of the carton price and disappears completely into a bowl this seasoned.
Hot honey is the fun ingredient and one bottle covers this batch three times over. If you already own honey and red pepper flakes, you can build your own and skip the specialty bottle entirely.
Five spice powder runs a few dollars a jar and lasts a year of cooking. Buy it at an international market where the same jar often costs half what the grocery store spice aisle charges.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the mushrooms thick. Thin slices vanish into a broth like this, and you want them to stay recognizable in the bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it into crumbles, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes without stirring much, so they release their water and then start to brown instead of steam.
Add the minced garlic and the five spice powder and stir for one minute. This blooming step wakes the spice up, and it is the whole reason this bowl tastes like more than salty broth.
Pour in the chicken broth, season with salt and black pepper, and simmer 15 minutes so the flavors marry.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat and taste. It should read savory first and sweet second.
Boil the lo mein noodles just short of done, drain them, rinse them cold so they stop cooking, and move them into your weighed pot.
portion_html: Set the pot of noodles on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. That is the noodle bed for each container. Ladle the turkey, mushrooms, and broth evenly across all 14 and top each with sliced green onions. Every bowl lands at 561 calories and 34 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from jennieo.com, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: A five spice noodle bowl for about $4.84 a serving (at everyday cost). This is one of hundreds. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, all for $1 a month.

head.description: Five spice turkey noodle bowls: ground turkey and mushrooms in five spice broth with hot honey over lo mein. 561 calories, 34g protein, about $4.84 a bowl (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: five spice turkey, noodle bowl, turkey meal prep, budget meal prep, hot honey noodles, mushroom noodle soup
steps: Brown the ground turkey in olive oil to 165F.
Add the mushrooms and cook 6 minutes until browned.
Add garlic and five spice powder and bloom one minute, then add the chicken broth and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the hot honey off the heat.
Cook and rinse the noodles, portion by weight into 14 containers, and ladle the broth over the top.
